SAGGLE ROC

Decision advantage from the deckplate up.

The Surface Analytics Group delivers analytics to the TYCOM and the surface fleet. Our team pairs technical experts with domain SMEs to turn fleet data into action.

The Problem

Two challenges stand between ships and current, accurate information

Streamlining Eight O'Clock report generation
Heavy manual effort pulls department heads and their teams away from warfighting work
Accessing up-to-date information in bandwidth-limited environments
Constrained connectivity slows how fast current data reaches the ship

SAGGLE ROC addresses both with one tool, built around the Eight O'Clock report.

Use Case

The Eight O'Clock report: the CO's daily picture of the ship

What it is

  • A formal end-of-day brief from department heads to the CO at about 2000
  • Covers PMT status (personnel, material, training) by department: Engineering, Operations, Combat Systems, Weapons and Supply
  • Routed through the XO or CDO
  • Typically completed by department heads or their subordinates

The challenge

  • Significant manual effort every day
  • Error-prone, given the manual process
  • Limited trend visibility over time
  • Cross-department blind spots

Much of the underlying data already lives in authoritative systems of record. It can be aggregated and shared out to automate most of the process.

Platform

Path 1 · Palantir Foundry: integrate and visualize PMT data

Why Foundry

  • Build operational apps quickly, without custom front-end code
  • Unify multiple data sources in one governed data model
  • Built-in access controls and data lineage
  • Short iteration loops with real users

What we used it for

  • Integrating PMT data from authoritative systems of record
  • Visualizing status by department, designed around the Eight O'Clock report
  • Workshop modules for department heads and triads to brief status
  • Trend and cross-department visibility

The same data also feeds Path 2, the low-bandwidth solution, for ships that cannot access Foundry.

Edge · Deep in the Rock

Path 2 · Low bandwidth: what if you can't access Foundry?

1Shore-sideAggregates data from authoritative systems of record and packages it into small data packets
2TransferSmall files travel over channels the ship already uses: email, Teams messages or naval message traffic
3ShipAn HTML tool, installed on a local computer, ingests each packet and presents the report, with no cloud connection required

Built for disconnected, intermittent and limited (DDIL) conditions: HTML files are sent to the ship once, then kept current with small data packets.

Impact

Reclaiming time for warfighting readiness

2.5 hrssaved per day of manual administrative burden
17+ hrsreclaimed per week for combat readiness, tactical training and maintenance
912+ hrsof deckplate time reclaimed per ship annually

Basis: 0.5 hours per department × 5 departments on a DDG = 2.5 hours per day. Also gives the commanding officer a highly accurate, near-real-time readiness picture.

Before

  • All-hands evolution: each department manually gathers PMT data from onboard databases
  • Data re-entered into spreadsheets and documents

After

  • Payload ingested locally; system statuses auto-populate
  • Departments review and brief instead of compile

Looking Ahead · Back to the Rock

What we learned and where we go next

Lessons learned

  • Data integration is the hard part: plan for it early
  • Connectivity dependence is a real risk: we relied fully on Wi-Fi
  • Token limits shape design: build with them in mind

Next steps

  • Add more data sources and functionality
  • Create a bidirectional flow of data between ship and shore
  • Build with real data
  • Package the HTML with Forge to meet cybersecurity requirements
Conclusion · Dance your cares away

Current information, wherever the ship is

  • The Eight O'Clock report is essential, and today it takes too much manual effort to produce
  • SAGGLE ROC streamlines report generation and delivers up-to-date information in bandwidth-limited environments
  • Standardized products give the fleet a shared view of status and trends
  • Ready to use on an actual ship today, with a clear path to more data and two-way flow
